_doc: Hand-read class of every claim that names a road (or a route) on the line of command of an undrawn leaf unit, for the sibling-road rule (DEC-015, tools/sibling-rule.mjs). The claims are the rows of APPROACH-AUDIT.md (the claims the audit examined); the class says what the printed words are: a place or movement inside the field, an order, no road, a compiler's gloss, an earlier march, a road the repository cannot place, another road of approach, a road outside the loaded ground, or a disagreement. A class in `blocks` stops the sibling rule for every unit under the claim. `by_code` is the default class of an audit code; `claims` overrides it for a claim (and, with `code`, names the reason shown when the claim blocks) and carries the note of the claims that sit on the line of command of a unit the rule draws (each of those was read in full; tests/sibling.test.mjs checks that none is missing). No claim here is a road of approach: a road of approach is a record of data/placement.json or data/placement-claims.json.

classes.in_field: the road named is where the unit stood or moved after it was on the field (a line along a road, a crossing, a battery by the pike): a place or a movement inside the field, not a road of approach
classes.order: a dispatch or an order printed as a movement (what a commander told another to do): not the road a unit marched on to the field
classes.no_road: the passage names no road (a direction, a town, “the road”, “road not named”)
classes.gloss: the road stands only in the compiler’s bracketed gloss or summary, not in the claim’s printed words (a bracketed gloss is never evidence); it names no road other than the sibling road
classes.unverifiable: an inferred claim with no verbatim quote: the road cannot be checked against printed words; it names no road other than the sibling road
classes.earlier: a march before the battle (outside the loaded ground), not the approach to the field
classes.another_place: the road named is a road of another place (the road to Carlisle from Chambersburg), not the gazetteer road of the same name
classes.not_the_unit: a move of the wagon train or its guard, not the approach of the unit’s line
classes.divisions_differ: a statement that different divisions of the corps took different roads: it is evidence that the sibling formations disagree, not a road of approach for the unit
classes.unplaceable: a report of the line of command names a road or a route that the repository cannot place (the road from Scotland, the route by Horner’s Mill, a railroad, a road named only by a village or a mill): none is guessed
classes.other_approach: a report of the line of command names another road of approach than the sibling road
classes.outside_ground: a road of approach is printed for the line of command but it does not cross the loaded ground (Black Horse Tavern Road)
classes.disagree: the reports of the same formation print different roads; none is chosen
classes.brigades_differ: a report of the line of command prints a continuation of the march that differs from that of another brigade of the same division (one turns off a pike, the other goes left past a hill): evidence that the formations disagree, not a road of approach for the unit; it does not block the sibling rule (the formations' own roads are the siblings)

POS-A-CV1-038.note: Howard to Reynolds, 1 July (OR27-3-D0959 p. 457): one division on the road Reynolds took, “the balance of the corps on the road past Horner’s Mills”. A road named by a mill: the repository holds no such road (road-concordance RC-07, unresolved). It stands on the line of command of every Eleventh Corps unit, so the corps stays open (brief sibling-roads, rule 1).
